content.title: Oregon State women's basketball eliminated by Wisconsin in WBIT  - Columbia County Spotlight
content.text: Published 9:02 pm Thursday, March 19, 2026 The season officially ended Thursday for Oregon State women’s basketball, falling 62-58 to No. 3 Wisconsin in the first round of the WBIT at Gill Coliseum in Corvallis. The Badgers (14-17) snapped a 10-game skid with the win, dominating the Beavers (23-12) in the paint. Oregon State conceded 32 points in the paint to Wisconsin, and the Badgers grabbed eight more rebounds (36) than their first-round host (28). “Tough loss, for sure. Don’t want things to end before it has to (but) Wisconsin played a really good game,” Oregon State head coach Scott Rueck said. “(They’re) a good team, obviously, big-time battle-tested. You look at (the Badgers’) last two months and who they’ve been playing against, it was evident tonight. They were really imposing at the rim, disruptive defensive and hit some timely shots.” Wisconsin caught Oregon State on its heels early, carrying a 15-10 lead through the first quarter and a 31-22 lead at halftime. The Beavers came out of the gate shooting cold, hitting just four of their 16 attempts from the field in the first 10 minutes. They found more life in the second quarter, hitting 41.7% (5-for-12) of their shots, but Wisconsin’s own hot shooting (7-for-11) and dominance on the glass (eight boards to Oregon State’s three) kept Oregon State at arm’s length. That was, until the second half got underway. Bolden’s dominant third quarter wills Beavers back Oregon State’s senior guard, Tiara Bolden, took the game over in the opening minutes of the second half and willed the Beavers back into the mix. The Eugene native scored 10 points within the first five minutes of the third and led Oregon State to a 21-point quarter. “I mean, in the first half, I feel like I was a little shaken (from) the pressure I put on myself,” Bolden said. “After experiencing that, being able to take a deep breath (helped me) reset and show out.” When it was all said and done in her final collegiate game, Bolden led the Beavers with 23 points. “Tiara kind of took the game over it seemed in that third quarter and willed us back in,” Rueck said. “So, it was one of the more enjoyable stretches of the season for us — that third-quarter run to get back in it… Just found a way to stay in it until the end, give ourselves a chance in the last minute. I was really proud of that effort. It was really on-brand for who this team is. We’ve just been a tough out every night and proved it again tonight. We were a tough out.” Bolden’s final basket of the night, a 3-pointer with less than three minutes to go, brought Oregon State within one. It was as close as the Beavers got in the fourth quarter. Though the two teams traded the lead five times overall and Oregon State outscored the Badgers in the second half, Wisconsin’s 13 fourth-quarter points were enough to hold on for the win. Wisconsin advances to round two of the WBIT, heading to Coral Gables, Florida, to play No. 2 Miami (18-14) on Sunday, March 22. Miami defeated Georgia Southern, 82-56, to advance. Tipoff between the Hurricanes and Badgers is to be announced. Final send off for Oregon State’s seniors The loss ends the collegiate careers of five Beavers — Bolden, forward Susana Yepes, and centers Lizzy Williamson and Nene Sow. Bolden and Sow, who spoke postgame, both thanked Oregon State fans — who showed up 2,014-fans deep for first-round matchup. “For me, as an international, I feel like (Gill Coliseum) has always been my home away from home,” Sow, a native Belgian, said. “So, being able to play here one more time, it was just playing at home one last time before going home.” “Beaver Nation shows up for us, every single time,” Bolden added. “That’s just something so special about Corvallis. And the fact I was able to play with my teammates here one more time after senior night, it was super special. (Being) surrounded by my friends and family, for me, meant everything.”
